response.text: Along Managua's broad promenade, the four duck their heads as one adjusts a woven palm sunshield over her companion's shoulders, while another feigns a pout at a passing kite that briefly steals her friend's attention. One delivers a swift cheek peck to the pouting woman, then all four interlock elbows and pivot into a tight, giggling circle, their high-collared guayabera dresses flaring as they step together in perfect unison.

On Granada's sun-dappled Calle La Calzada, they pause before a mustard-yellow facade to swap oversized tortoiseshell sunglasses, as one gently brushes a fallen jacaranda bloom from another's nape with a protective murmur. A third playfully blocks the view of Mombacho with her open hand, claiming the volcano's silhouette for herself, but the brushed woman pecks her on the cheek and all four immediately link wrists, stepping forward in a single-file chain that weaves between the colorful columns.

On Ometepe's dry lakeside terrace, they set down hand-painted ceramic fans and kneel to trace twin volcanic shapes in the dust with their fingertips, while one steadies another's swaying straw hat against a gust off the lake. A rival mock-groans and snatches the tracing stick, insisting her own rendition is sharper, yet receives a quick peck on the jaw before all four rise and clasp forearms, each placing a smooth obsidian stone atop the others' hands in a silent pact.

Centered on Laguna de Apoyo's broad mirador, they turn their backs to the gentle slope and point past the forested rim, as one tucks a stray braid behind her friend's ear and pulls the collar of her stark-white tunic higher against a breeze. Another jokingly steps between two who are sharing binoculars, but after a playful peck lands on her cheek, all four gather shoulder-to-shoulder and exchange their draped indigo shawls, each knotting the fabric around a different waist in a round of shared symmetry.
